trust_decision.summary: _sanitizeElements decides whether a node survives and then hands it to the user's afterSanitizeElements policy hook; for a custom element kept via CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING.tagNameCheck it returns early from _sanitizeDisallowedNode and the user's hook-layered policy is never applied to it.

landing_point.why: The summary names CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING and afterSanitizeElements; the only early return that skips the hook for kept custom elements is the _sanitizeDisallowedNode call in _sanitizeElements, and the docblock at src/purify.ts:1661-1666 even states the skip.

fix_sites.entry_point: DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty, {CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING}) with an afterSanitizeElements hook registered via DOMPurify.addHook; reached from main walk (src/purify.ts:2506) and from template-content/shadow walks (src/purify.ts:2188)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The pinned docblock at src/purify.ts:1663-1665 says skipping afterSanitizeElements for kept custom elements is intentional, so a solver could argue the behaviour is by design; but this argues against fixing the landing point itself, not a second route.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The namespace and fallback-tag (noscript/noembed/noframes) removal checks must stay skipped for kept custom elements, and attributes of kept custom elements must still be sanitized by _sanitizeAttributes; an over-broad fix that routes kept custom elements through the full normal tail could change removal decisions, and a fix that runs the hook on removed nodes would hand detached nodes to the hook.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A dedicated keep-path for custom elements inside the template-content/shadow walk (_sanitizeShadowDOM) that returns before afterSanitizeElements
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The shadow walk already has its own hook (uponSanitizeShadowNode) and loop; a maintainer optimising or specialising shadow handling could inline custom-element keeping there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An EXTRA_ELEMENT_HANDLING.tagCheck keep path that returns false early instead of falling through to the hook tail
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: tagCheck is a second user-configurable allow route next to the same condition; a maintainer could give it an early return mirroring the custom-element keep.

O9_family: XSS / sanitizer policy-hook bypass (incomplete hook lifecycle for allowlisted custom elements)
